newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed more Warehousing shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed more Warehousing shares.

text.p: The state Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) will shed in May 80 million Public Warehousing Co shares by public subscription at 370 fils ($1.22) a share.
Warehousing shares were trading on Monday around 410 fils after opening at 415, reaching a daily high of 420. In March the share reached a new record high of 465 fils.
The subscription opens May 4 and closes on May 14, newspapers quoted an official announcement.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the Kuwait Stock Exchange.
Earlier in April, KIA, the state investment arm which has been leading a privatisation programme, shed 40 million Warehousing shares by auction.
The state had a 49 percent stake Warehousing. The latest subscription represents 30 percent of the firm's 269.34 million issued shares.
The 18-year-old firm's net profit rose to 16.5 percent to 5.45 million dinars in 1996 and dividends climbed 14.3 percent to fils per share. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
